What is the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis code for this patient?

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [REDACTED]
Sex: Male
Date of Admission: [REDACTED]
Date of Discharge: [REDACTED]

Hospital Course:

The patient, an 18-year-old male with no significant past medical history, was admitted to the emergency department with complaints of suprapubic and periumbilical pain, accompanied by nausea for one day. Physical examination revealed mild tenderness to palpation in the periumbilical, right lower quadrant, and left upper quadrant regions. Respiratory rate, heart rate, and blood pressure were within normal limits, but complete blood count revealed leukocytosis with a left shift.

A CT exam was performed to rule out any underlying causes of the aforementioned symptoms, demonstrating a dilated and hyperenhancing retrocecal appendix containing a form of calcified materials within it. Moreover, small air collections were identified anterior to the right and left common iliac arteries, and posterior to both psoas muscles in the retroperitoneal cavity of the abdomen.

The patient was taken to the operating room for an appendectomy, during which an additional inflamed appendix, and evidence of minor perforation into the retroperitoneum were found. Surgical team continued with appendectomy in view of inferior incision area revealing no pathologic process in the retroperitoneal cavity.

The patient was monitored in the post-operative care unit and demonstrated no post-operative complications. The patient was discharged the following day in stable condition.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Instructions:

The patient is advised to take all prescribed medications and attend follow-up appointments as scheduled. Discharge instructions and the post-operative care plan have been explained to the patient in detail before being discharged.

text:
**Principal diagnosis code: K35.32 – Acute appendicitis with perforation and localised peritonitis, without generalised peritonitis**

This is my best coding judgement from the summary. The diagnosis section was withheld, so it should be confirmed against the full record.

**Rationale**
- The reason for admission and surgery was acute appendicitis. The patient had periumbilical and right lower quadrant pain, leukocytosis with left shift, and a dilated, hyperenhancing appendix on CT. An appendicolith was also present (calcified material within the appendix).
- At surgery there was inflamed appendix with perforation into the retroperitoneum. The CT showed retroperitoneal air collections, which fits the perforation.
- Perforation of the appendix with local peritoneal involvement is classified under K35.3. The ICD-10-AM 11th edition splits this into K35.30 (acute appendicitis with localised peritonitis), K35.31 (acute appendicitis with perforation and localised peritonitis) and K35.32 (acute appendicitis with perforation and localised peritonitis, without generalised peritonitis), depending on the edition. Check the code set your facility uses.
- The summary does not describe generalised peritonitis or an abscess. The surgeons found no pathological process in the retroperitoneal cavity, so K35.2 (generalised peritonitis) and K35.33 (abscess) do not apply.

**Caveats**
- If the surgeon documented only "acute appendicitis" without perforation or peritonitis, the code would be K35.8 (other and unspecified acute appendicitis). Coders cannot assume peritonitis from perforation alone, so a query to the clinician may be needed.
- The "additional inflamed appendix" wording is ambiguous. It is probably a documentation error, since duplicate appendix is rare, and it should be clarified. If a true duplicate appendix (Q43.8) were documented, it would be an additional code.
- The procedure would be coded separately as an appendicectomy (ACHI block 926).
